title: Minimum Cost to Equalize Arrays Using Swaps
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal size, you can swap elements within the same array or between the arrays.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal size, you can swap elements within the same array or between the arrays. Swapping within an array is free, while swapping between arrays incurs a cost of 1 per operation. Determine the minimum cost to make both arrays identical, or return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 have equal positive length.
Reordering within either array is free; swapping one element between arrays costs one.
Return the minimum cross-array swaps needed to make their multisets equal, or -1.
reference_solution:
def minimum_cross_swaps_to_equal(nums1,nums2):
    from collections import Counter
    remaining=Counter(nums2);excess=Counter()
    for value in nums1:
        if remaining[value]:remaining[value]-=1
        else:excess[value]+=1
    answer=0
    for count in excess.values():
        if count%2:return -1
        answer+=count//2
    if any(count%2 for count in remaining.values()):return -1
    return answer

Every combined multiplicity must be even; half of each even excess in nums1 must cross and determines the cost.
One cross swap fixes one needed transfer in each direction, so the counted nums1 transfers are both achievable and necessary.
